numpy_residual_trend_decomposition.mechanism_summary: np.matmul(u_arr, s_np) and (v_arr - u_arr @ s_np) alone show zero positive weight trend. Almost the entire ~0.3 us residual trend comes from signed floor-modulo (`diff % q64`): at weight=0, diff = v_arr >= 0 (0% negative), whereas at weight=8 ~34% of diff entries are negative; NumPy int64 remainder executes a sign-fixup branch when the dividend is negative, causing branch mispredictions as negative elements increase. Adding a non-negative offset (+n*q64) before `% q64` eliminates the modulo trend; the remaining ~0.03 us difference in full expressions comes from np.asarray(s) unpacking Python int 0 vs +/-1. Across full 40 us decrypt_it_constant_time calls, this sub-microsecond micro-trend is buried beneath wrapper/OS jitter (5,000-trial Spearman rho=-0.0258, p=0.068).
